summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with dyspnea, nonproductive cough, and wheezing, initially managed as a COPD exacerbation with antibiotics and steroids. She developed progressive hypoxia and pulmonary edema, requiring ICU admission and aggressive diuresis resulting in 14 liters of fluid removal. Urinalysis and culture confirmed a UTI with Enterococcus, treated with cefpodoxime. Her condition stabilized, and she was transitioned to the medical ward. A right heart catheterization was considered to evaluate for pulmonary hypertension due to unclear etiology of pulmonary edema, but the patient declined prior to the procedure, and it was canceled. She improved clinically, was ambulatory and afebrile, saturating 95% on room air at discharge. She was discharged home with home health services, new medication adjustments including a diuretic and inhalers, and follow-up arranged with her primary care provider and pulmonologist to determine need for outpatient cardiac evaluation.
